frontier.hypothesis: F6 (NEW, UNMEASURED LEAD - do this FIRST) - campaign wsA's best find, output-383-1 (permuter 383 vs base 468), may be a sub-16 form; it was never re-measured because WSL died before it surfaced.
frontier.mechanism: It combines two constructs the session never tested together: (a) `count = D_800A2668 != 0;` - the guard staged through the s32 local and then overwritten with the table length inside the branch. This is a cast-free relative of session 3's guard carry, sits inside the frozen 'variable reuse for codegen control' family, and was never tried in combination with this session's do-while(0) wrap; by the same loop-depth/live-length arithmetic it should raise count's live_length (which is the direction F4b needs) rather than p's refs. (b) `D_800A2668++; D_800A2668--;` - a redundant RMW pair on the guard global. (b) is a FIRST REACH of a family nothing in the frozen SOTN list covers: if GCC folds the pair (likely - two adjacent RMWs on the same non-volatile location with nothing between them) it emits no bytes and its only function is to move GCC's analysis, failing checklist T1 and T2; if it does not fold it stores to a global the target never stores to, which is a behavioural difference rather than a match.
frontier.next_probe: Measure `memory/grind/motion_Close/unmeasured_lead_s4_383.c` with `sandbox motion_Close --disable all` plus the instrumented cc1, then DECOMPOSE it: (a) alone, (b) alone, (a) composed with this session's `do { p = &D_8008D070; } while (0);` wrap, and (a) with p assigned first (the F4b shape). Report the allocno table per form. If (b) proves load-bearing, emit `ruling-request` - do not self-approve it. NOTE: WSL was left wedged at the end of session 4 (Wsl/Service/E_UNEXPECTED, host reboot likely needed); confirm the toolchain is healthy before trusting any measurement.

frontier.hypothesis: F5 (NEW, largest never-probed bucket) - the guard-load / jalr temp can be moved from $v0 to the target's $t0, worth 2 points.
frontier.mechanism: Both the D_800A2668 guard load and the indirect call target land in $v0 in every form measured across four sessions, while the target uses $t0 for both. This is a local-alloc (local-alloc.c) decision over call-clobbered registers, not a global.c one, so none of the allocno-priority levers worked on it so far touch it — and no session has ever read the .lreg dump for these pseudos. It is the only remaining non-frame bucket that is neither dead-by-H1 nor the F4 order bind.
frontier.next_probe: Compile the candidate with `-da` and read the .lreg local-alloc dump for the guard pseudo and the call-target pseudo: what makes local-alloc prefer $v0, and does the preference come from a copy-preference to the return register or from the register-class scan order? Then sweep forms that give the guard value and the call target different lifetimes (guard consumed before the frame exists, call target read into a variable used after the call, a second call-clobbered value live across the guard test) and read the dump per form. Both halves must move together — the target uses $t0 for the load AND the jalr.

frontier.hypothesis: F4b (carried forward, still unprobed) - lengthen count's live range instead of moving statements, so p-first emission order and p's priority win can hold at once (worth the last 2 positional points).
frontier.mechanism: Assigning p before count fails only because count is born one statement later, shortening its live_length 8 -> 7 and RAISING its priority to 38571. If count's live range can be lengthened back to 8+ without adding a count reference - e.g. by an intervening real computation that the target also performs, so count spans it - the p-first order and p's 34285 could hold simultaneously. Alternatively give p ~11 weighted references inside its existing range (a second wrapped reference is worth 2 each), which beats 38571 at 11/8 = 41250.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate the insns the target places between the guard branch and the loop (insns 8-13) and test body arrangements that make count live across each in turn; measure score + allocno table per arrangement. In parallel, sweep p-first forms carrying two or three wrapped p references (each worth 2 by loop-depth weighting) and check whether p can reach 11 weighted refs at live_length 8 without emitting a byte.
